title: perf(formatter): build the math exclusion ranges once per line
issue_body:
## What and why

Codex found this on #53 after it merged: span protection is quadratic on a line that holds link destinations, display math and at least two backtick runs. For each `$$...$$` match, the code-span pass rebuilt and sorted the whole list of link-destination and URL ranges, so a 104 KB line took about 5 seconds here (11 seconds on Codex's machine). That line is under the 200 KB size cap, and the hook formats synchronously, so the reply was held up for that long.

The merged range list is now built once per line and reused for every math match. On the same 104 KB line, formatting drops from 5.21 s to 0.09 s.

## How to test

```
cd lyre
uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest tests/formatter/test_performance.py
```

The new test, `test_link_targets_math_and_code_runs_scale_linearly`, failed before the fix. It checks that quadrupling the input stays under 8 times the time, plus an absolute 2 s ceiling on the 104 KB line.

## Platforms tested

Windows 11, Python 3.14.9: 3,363 passed, 4 skipped. Ruff 0.15.10 passes.

## Related issues

Follows #53 (review finding 4545875805).

@@ -40,6 +40,18 @@ def test_ac9_twenty_kb_mixed_reply_within_budget():
     assert _best_of(_fixture(20_000)) < BUDGET_S
 
 
+def test_link_targets_math_and_code_runs_scale_linearly():
+    # Link destinations, display math and two backtick runs on one line used to rebuild the
+    # exclusion ranges once per math span, so a 104 KB line took several seconds.
+    def reply(n: int) -> str:
+        return "[a](b) " * n + "$$x$$ " * n + "`code` `more`"
+
+    small = _best_of(reply(2_000), runs=1)
+    large = _best_of(reply(8_000), runs=1)
+    assert large < 2.0
+    assert large < 8 * max(small, 0.01)  # 4x the input: linear is ~4x, quadratic ~16x
+
+

     text = _fixture(20_000) * 50
     assert len(text.encode()) > 200_000

title: fix(formatter): keep titled links and protect inline math
issue_body:
## What and why

Two inputs lost information on the way to speech.

- **Titled links.** `[policy](https://example.test "Do not share externally")` became `policy, link: https://example.test`, dropping the title. A link or image whose target has a title (`"..."`, `'...'` or `(...)`, or any other text after the destination) is now left exactly as written, label included, on both profiles. Span protection stashes the whole construct (a linked image counts as one unit when either target has a title), and the link rule checks again as a backstop. Emphasis around the link is still removed. Untitled links behave as before.
- **Inline math.** On `plain`, `$a*b*c$` became `$abc$` and `\(a*b*c\)` became `\(abc\)`. One-line inline math is now a protected span: `$$...$$` (as before), `\(...\)`, `\[...\]`, and tight `$...$` following Pandoc's `tex_math_dollars` rule (a non-space after the opening `$`, a non-space before the closing `$`, no digit right after it, no line break). Prices stay prose: `Price is $5 and *really* $10.` still becomes `Price is $5 and really $10.`, and the same holds for `$5-$10`, `$5/$10` and `costs $3.50, about $4`.
  - An escaped opener (`\$`, `\\(`) never starts math. The search then moves on one character, so a second pass finds the same math as the first.
  - Math never reaches into a link destination or a bare URL.
  - Code spans win over the new forms, and backticks pair first as before. Only `$$` keeps its earlier precedence over backticks.
  - Matching is linear in line length:
    - A `$` body never contains a `$`, escaped or not, so `$a\$b$` is not math and stays prose (fail-open).
    - A `\(` body never contains `\(` or `\)`, and a `\[` body never contains `\[` or `\]`.
    - Each position is tried as a math start at most once, including after a rejected match.
- **Reference-definition titles.** In `[r]: https://x.test/a "t *x*"`, the destination and a title on the same line are protected together. Before, `plain` gave `"t x"`, as main still does. A title on the next line is still prose (recorded in ADR 0009 and R8).

ADR 0009 records the decision, the dollar rule, what is still not protected (multi-line `\[ ... \]` and `\( ... \)`, `$a\$b$`, next-line reference titles, `\begin{...}` outside `$$`, `$ x $`, link labels with nested brackets) and the costs. Spec step 2, the non-goals, R8 and `lyre/README.md` now list exactly what is protected.

## How to test

From `lyre/`:

```
uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest
uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest tests/formatter/test_titles_and_math.py tests/formatter/test_performance.py
```

From the repo root: `uvx ruff@0.15.10 check .`

New timing tests in `tests/formatter/test_performance.py` cover adversarial lines: escaped dollars, `$` openers before spaces, unclosed and escaped `\(`/`\[`, and matches rejected into destinations or URLs. They check that 4x the input takes under 8x the time, with an absolute ceiling. They also check that a 17.6 KB line of escaped prices stays within the 100 ms budget.

New golden case: `tests/golden/cases/33-titled-links-and-inline-math.md`. Running `python tests/golden/update_golden.py` changes no other expected file.

## Platforms tested

- Windows 11, Python 3.14.9, merged with main (including #58): 3445 passed, 4 skipped. Ruff reports all checks passed.
- Timings, best of 3, before -> after this fix:
  - `'x \$5 ' * 8000`: 5.88 s -> 0.029 s (2000/4000/8000 copies now take 0.007/0.014/0.029 s).
  - `'Costs \$5 each, ' * 1100` (17.6 KB): 0.27 s -> 0.007 s.
  - Escaped `\\( a ` x 8000 plus a closing `\)`: 19 s -> 0.026 s. The `\\[` analogue now takes 0.027 s.
- Fuzz, `LYRE_FUZZ_SEED=150 LYRE_FUZZ_CASES=2000`: 4003 passed, 2 failed (seed 1435, both profiles). Seed 1435 belongs to a bug class main already has: after a list is rewritten, a code span pairs across lines and takes precedence over math. Main shows the same with ``"`\n- $$`✅$$"`` and ``"`\n- `✅`"``. Before this PR the seed did not reach that path; this PR does not fix it.
- Extended fuzz, seeds 0 to 5999, run before this fix: seed 4687 reached a second existing bug class, where Setext heading lines joined into one line form math. Main shows the same with `"x $$│\nمم$$a✅ש\n="`.

## Related issues

Follows #8

title: fix(formatter): keep emoji that Lyre has no word for
issue_body:
## What and why

Under the default `emoji_policy: words`, Lyre removed every emoji that was not a status emoji. That deleted meaning: `The answer is 🇫🇷, not 🇩🇪.` became `The answer is, not.`, `Use key 1️⃣ to continue.` became `Use key to continue.`, `Rated ⭐⭐⭐⭐ out of 5` became `Rated out of 5`, and `Temp 30°C ☀️ today` became `Temp 30°C today`. Because Hermes stores the rewrite, the model loses it too.

Now only the status emoji in the R4 table (done, failed, warning, red, yellow, green, pending) become words. Every other emoji is kept byte for byte, whole sequence included (ZWJ, skin tones, keycaps, tag flags, variation selectors). Screen readers speak their own names for them.

Decisions:
- **Mixed runs** keep their order: `✅ 🎉 ⚠️` -> `(done) 🎉 (warning)`, `✅🎉` -> `(done) 🎉`. Each status word gets one space on each side. Kept emoji keep the gaps they had to each other and to the text next to them (`*✅🎉hi*` -> `*(done) 🎉hi*`).
- **Runs with no status emoji** are left exactly as written, spacing included. The rule therefore does nothing on a second pass, so idempotency holds.
- **Decorative emoji** are kept too (`# 🚀 Deploy` -> `🚀 Deploy.` on plain). No test argued for an exception.
- **A line with an emoji and box drawing** (`🎉 ───`) is no longer removed under `words`, because with the emoji kept it is not drawing-only.
- `remove` still removes every emoji, status emoji included. The README and spec now say it loses information. `keep` still skips the rule.

Docs: ADR 0008 (keep emoji without a spoken word) is new and listed in the ADR index. Spec R4 drops the "any other emoji | removed" row and describes the new default and mixed runs. AC-4 is now `(done) 🎉`. AC-10 now forbids only status emoji under `words`, and every emoji under `remove`. Script detection no longer mentions decorative emoji removal. README "What changes", the non-Latin line, the settings list and the before/after example are updated, along with the test-evidence rows for AC-4 and AC-10. DESIGN.md does not describe removing emoji, so it is unchanged.

Tests rewritten or moved (they asserted removal of non-status emoji under `words`):
- `test_emoji.py`: `CASES` now expect the emoji kept, plus the four reproductions, mixed runs and a standalone skin tone. A new `REMOVE_CASES`/`test_remove_policy` holds the old removal expectations. These were rewritten: `test_link_label_keeps_url_emoji`, `test_non_latin_reply_keeps_every_emoji` (renamed), `test_more_emoji_presentations`, `test_text_default_base_with_skin_tone_is_one_unit` (renamed), `test_emoji_then_drawing_line_removed_in_one_pass`, `test_emoji_letter_does_not_count_as_script`, `test_emphasis_delimiters_beside_punctuation`, `test_supplementary_text_symbols`, the `**🎉 Hello**` case and the standalone skin tone test. The emphasis and spacing fuzz regressions (`test_emptied_emphasis_wrapper_is_removed`, `test_delimiters_of_neighbouring_spans_are_kept`, `test_original_pairing_survives_multiple_run_edits`, `test_run_between_word_and_emptied_wrapper_keeps_word_boundary`, `test_run_delimiters_use_original_line_context`) now run under `remove`, which is the path they cover. The intraword asterisk, underscore, strikethrough and nested delimiter tests now expect `words` to give the same output as `keep`. New: `test_words_without_status_emoji_matches_keep` runs the fuzz-found inputs and requires `words` output to equal `keep` output. Also new: `test_decorative_heading_emoji_is_kept`.
- `test_emoji_work.py`: the bounded-work tests run under `remove`. New: `test_many_status_emoji_runs_stay_bounded` for mixed runs under `words`.
- `test_lists.py`: `- 🎉 party` -> `2, 🎉 party`. The emptied-item case now uses `- ───`, and `- 🎉` keeps its emoji. Both unsafe-continuation tests run under `remove`, because under `words` the emoji line no longer empties.
- `test_review_followups.py`: under `words` the lone regional indicator is now kept.
- `test_verbosity.py`: emoji row is now `(done) done 🎉`.
- `test_properties.py`: AC-10 checks only status emoji under `words`. Two new properties: under `words` no emoji without a word is lost, and under `remove` no emoji is left.

Golden expectations regenerated: 05, 07, 10, 27 and 32 (both profiles) only gain the emoji that used to be removed. No code or URL bytes changed.

## How to test

From `lyre/`:

    uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest
    LYRE_FUZZ_CASES=3000 uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest tests/formatter/test_properties.py tests/formatter/test_fuzz.py

From the repo root: `uvx ruff@0.15.10 check .`

## Platforms tested

- Windows 11, Python 3.14.9: 4007 passed, 7 skipped, after merging origin/main (#58). The 3 new skips are `test_remove_policy` markdown cases that contain `*`, which is the same skip rule as `test_words_policy`.
- Fuzz with `LYRE_FUZZ_SEED=150 LYRE_FUZZ_CASES=2000` (properties and fuzz): 20005 passed.
- ruff 0.15.10: all checks passed.

Review follow-up, same PR:
- **Keycap emoji next to emphasis.** The `*` that starts a keycap emoji (`*` then U+FE0F and/or U+20E3, as in `*️⃣`) was taken as an emphasis delimiter and stripped, leaving an orphan U+FE0F U+20E3. For example, `Press *️⃣ for help*` became `Press \ufe0f\u20e3 for help`. The same bug was already on main under `keep`; this PR made it reachable by default. Fix: `mask_keycaps` in `emphasis.py` swaps each keycap `*` for a private-use character that is not in the text before pairing, then puts the `*` back. Offsets do not change, so the emoji rule uses it for delimiter edges too. A `#` keycap is never a heading marker either: the ATX heading rule needs a space after `#`. New tests: `test_keycap_survives_emphasis_whole` (6 keycaps × 10 lines × both profiles × words and keep, byte for byte and idempotent) and `test_keycap_beside_emphasis_exact`.
- **Status emoji with a skin tone** (`✅🏻 ok`) becomes `(done) ok` again: modifiers are stripped before the status lookup (`test_status_emoji_with_skin_tone_becomes_word`).
- **Regression tests for mixed runs beside delimiters:** `un*🎉✅believ*able`, `*one*🎉✅**two**`, `hi✅**🎉**there` and three more, on both profiles. Each checks idempotence and that no emoji is lost (`test_mixed_runs_beside_delimiters`).
- Spec: R1 now says a keycap's `*` is never a delimiter, and R4 now says a status emoji with a skin tone still becomes its word.
- Known issue, already on main and not fixed here: under `remove`, `[🎉](https://e.test/a)` is not idempotent. The first pass gives `🎉, link: https://e.test/a` and the second gives `, link: https://e.test/a`. Tracked in #43.

## Related issues

title: feat(formatter): drop the backslash from prose escapes that cannot become markup
issue_body:
## What and why

TalkBack reads every backslash that reaches the screen, and Telegram, WhatsApp, Slack and plain clients show a Markdown escape in prose (`2 \* 3`) with its backslash. This adds spec rule R10 (`lyre/formatter/rules/escapes.py`, ADR 0011). It runs last on both profiles and removes the backslash only when the escaped character stands alone between two words: a space or tab on each side, and a letter or digit next on each side.

- **Removed** (both profiles): `\*`, `\_`, `\~`, `\#`, `\-`, `\+`, `\=`, `\>`, `\<`, `\&`, `\!`, `\(`, `\)`, `\.`, `\,`, `\;`, `\:`, `\?`, `\/`, `\%`, `\@`, `\^`, `\{`, `\}`, `\"`, `\'`, but only between two words (`2 \* 3` becomes `2 * 3`). With whitespace on both sides the character is not flanking, so it cannot open or close emphasis or strikethrough. Because a word comes before it, it cannot be at the start of a line, list item, quote or cell.
- **`*`, `_` and `~` must also be the only one on their line.** The escape goes only if no other copy of that character remains on the line, whether bare, escaped, or inside code, a URL or a link destination. Otherwise every escape of that character on the line stays. Telegram's adapter in Hermes v0.23.0 (the plugin's minimum version) pairs any two asterisks on a line as italics, ignoring spaces and backslashes. So `2 \* 3 \* 4`, `2 \* 3 and retry\*limit`, `2 \* 3 and 4 * 5` and `a \_ b \_ c` keep their backslashes. No messaging adapter in either version pairs them across lines, so `2 \* 3 = 6` on one line and `4 \* 5 = 20` on the next both lose theirs. Core's plain-text formatter (SMS, iMessage) does pair `*` across lines and ignores backslashes, but it already dropped those asterisks before (it left `2 \ 3`).
- **The line that counts is the output line.** R6 speaks a table row as one line that joins the column names and all of the row's cells. Cells therefore go through every inline rule except R10, and R6 then runs R10 on each spoken line it builds. `| 2 \* 3 | 4 \* 5 |` keeps both backslashes; `| 2 \* 3 | x |` loses one. Other places that join text keep each piece on its own line (list items, code labels, `Quote:`) or already run the inline rules on the joined text (Setext headings, link text). An independent review found this. Other characters do not need to be unique: `a \# b \# c` becomes `a # b # c`.
- **Always kept:** `` \` `` (code-span pairing), `\[` and `\]` (links), `\|` (table cells), `\$` (math in some apps) and `\\` (removing one would still leave a backslash).
- **Kept by position:** in-word (`retry\*limit`), paired (`\_name\_`, `\*literal\*`), at the start of a line or after a list, quote or ordered marker (`\# x`, `- \* x`, `1. \* x`), next to non-word characters (`(2) \* 3`, `2 \* (3)`), with no space on one side (`2 \*3`), next to another escape (`2 \* \* 3`) and at the end of a line.
- Code spans, fenced and indented code, math, URLs (including those that contain a backslash), link destinations and HTML tags are protected first and stay byte-identical.
- An escape that emoji removal exposes, for example a lone backslash before an emoji and `)`, goes through the same test on the first pass. A fuzz sweep found this case.

Downstream (checked against the real adapters at Hermes v0.23.0 and v0.23.1): on v0.23.1, Telegram's MarkdownV2 conversion escapes the backslash itself, so it displayed `2 \* 3`. A bare `2 * 3` is escaped by the adapter and shown as `2 * 3`. On v0.23.0, Telegram pairs asterisks itself, which is why the one-per-line condition above exists. A round-trip test now checks that, on every adapter, Lyre's output gets no pairing the reply as written would not get. WhatsApp and Slack pass the text through. Discord already hid the escape and shows the bare character the same way. Core's plain-text formatter (SMS, iMessage) drops any two `*` in a message, on one line or across lines, whether or not they have backslashes, so the result there is no worse. On Telegram with Hermes v0.23.0, a spoken table row with two `*` from different cells is shown in italics even when both keep their backslashes, because that adapter ignores backslashes. That comes from R6 joining cells; R10 neither causes it nor makes it worse. A round-trip test checks this.

Known gaps that already existed (not caused by this rule, though more inputs now reach them because more lines change): a changed paragraph line directly above a line indented by four or more columns gains a blank line, so the second pass labels that line as code (reproduce with `w **b** 3\n\t1.` on plain or `w ~~b~~ 3\n\t1.` on either profile). List output can also change how an unmatched backtick pairs across lines (`` `\n- `w **b** 3` ``). Both need a fix in the core pipeline.

## How to test

From `lyre/`:

- `uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest`
- With Hermes importable: `PYTHONPATH=<hermes-agent>;<pytest libs> <hermes venv python> -m pytest` (adapter round trips, including `test_removed_escape_shows_the_bare_character` `test_lyre_adds_no_pairing_the_app_would_not_do_anyway` and `test_spoken_table_row_gets_no_pairing_from_removed_escapes`). Run it once against a checkout of Hermes v0.23.0 (CI's pinned ref `2bd378ed`) and once against current Hermes.
- `LYRE_FUZZ_SEED=150 LYRE_FUZZ_CASES=3000 ... pytest tests/formatter/test_fuzz.py tests/formatter/test_properties.py`
- `uvx ruff@0.15.10 check .`
- Golden corpus: `python tests/golden/update_golden.py` adds case 34-prose-escapes only, numbered 34 so it does not clash with case 33 from the titled links and math PR. The existing 32 cases do not change.

Manual and still to do: send `docs/baseline/probe-escapes.md` to Telegram with Lyre on and re-listen with TalkBack. Item 2's `2 \* 3` should no longer say "backslash". Items 1 and 3, and `\_not italic\_`, are expected to still say it.

## Platforms tested

- Windows 11, Python 3.14.9
- Merged with main (including the span-protection performance fix).
- Plain suite: 3543 passed, 4 skipped
- With the Hermes v0.23.0 adapters (release commit 2bd378ed, shallow checkout): 3675 passed, 3 skipped, 1 xfailed
- With the Hermes v0.23.1 adapters (local install): 3675 passed, 3 skipped, 1 xfailed
- Differential check over 6,000 generated replies (tables, lists, Setext and ATX headings, quotes, random escapes) on both profiles at every verbosity: wherever R10 removed a backslash from `*`, `_` or `~`, that character is alone on its output line.
- Wide fuzz sweep (seed 150, 3000 cases) and property tests passed: 24005 passed. An extra 20,000-case escape-focused sweep showed no new failure class.
- ruff 0.15.10: all checks passed. 20 KB worst-case escape inputs take 6 to 25 ms.
- TalkBack on Telegram: not tested yet.

## Related issues

Part of #51 (the TalkBack re-listen is pending)

title: Formatter: edge cases from the final review rounds
issue_body:
Review findings left open when the formatter stack merged. Each is a P2 edge case: a rare input keeps or loses some markup, or formats differently on a second pass. None of them raises an error, and the formatter returns the input unchanged on any internal failure.

Each finding's thread has the reproduction.

- [ ] #33: Protect display math opened immediately after a list marker (https://github.com/jzeng151/hermes-lyre/pull/33#discussion_r4541358966)
- [ ] #33: Keep inline-math matching within link-target boundaries (https://github.com/jzeng151/hermes-lyre/pull/33#discussion_r4541358977)
- [ ] #33: Exclude protected math contents from code-span openers (https://github.com/jzeng151/hermes-lyre/pull/33#discussion_r4541358986)
- [ ] #33: Handle tab-expanded whitespace after quote markers (https://github.com/jzeng151/hermes-lyre/pull/33#discussion_r4541358998)
- [ ] #33: Exclude thematic breaks from list tracking during protection (https://github.com/jzeng151/hermes-lyre/pull/33#discussion_r4541359012)
- [ ] #34: Handle nested strikethrough without leaving actionable delimiters (https://github.com/jzeng151/hermes-lyre/pull/34#discussion_r4541386559)
- [ ] #34: Separate the quote announcement from Setext-like contents (https://github.com/jzeng151/hermes-lyre/pull/34#discussion_r4541386566)
- [ ] #34: Allow literal single markers inside strong emphasis (https://github.com/jzeng151/hermes-lyre/pull/34#discussion_r4541386574)
- [ ] #35: Remove standalone regional indicators as well as flag pairs (https://github.com/jzeng151/hermes-lyre/pull/35#discussion_r4541349767)
- [ ] #36: Apply paragraph-interruption rules to nested markers (https://github.com/jzeng151/hermes-lyre/pull/36#discussion_r4541359817)
- [ ] #38: Separate list-owned code labels from preceding blockquotes (https://github.com/jzeng151/hermes-lyre/pull/38#discussion_r4542107912)
- [ ] Telegram: with Lyre on, the code language is heard twice (Lyre's `Python code, N lines:` label, then Telegram's own `Python` label). Found in the #2 baseline.



## Found while fixing the information-loss bugs

Idempotence gaps that already exist on `main`. Each shows up only on rare input, and none raises an error. The fuzz seeds come from `LYRE_FUZZ_CASES` runs with seeds 0 to 5999.

- [ ] Under `emoji_policy: remove`, removing an emoji can expose a list marker: `- - ☀️_** ☀️` gives `- -_**`, and the second pass gives `1 item.` then `1, -_**`.
- [ ] A rewritten list can change how an unmatched backtick pairs across lines: ``"`\n- `✅`"`` (plain).
- [ ] A Setext heading joins its lines, which can form math the separate lines did not, and script detection then flips between passes: `"x $$│\nمم$$a✅ש\n="`.
- [ ] A changed paragraph line above a line indented 4 or more columns gains a blank line, so the second pass labels it as code: `"w ~~b~~ 3\n\t1."`.
- [ ] Fuzz seeds that fail on `main`: 3264, 3908, 3956 and 4240.


- [ ] Under `emoji_policy: remove`, an emoji that is a whole link label is not idempotent: `[🎉](https://e.test/a)` gives `🎉, link: https://e.test/a`, and the second pass gives `, link: https://e.test/a`.

- [ ] A quote holding fenced code inside a list item gets its code labels only on the second pass, on both profiles: `- a` then a blank line, then `  > ```python`, `  > x = 1`, `  > ````.

- [ ] Telegram on Hermes v0.23.0 only: a spoken table row joins its cells on one line, and that adapter pairs any two `*` on a line even when they are escaped. `| 2 \* 3 | 4 \* 5 |` is read as `Row 1: A 2 \* 3, B 4 \* 5.`, and Telegram shows the middle as italics. Later Hermes versions escape the asterisks instead.

---
PR Context (#50):
## What and why

Fixes everything deferred to #43: the 11 review findings left open when the formatter stack merged, and the random-character inputs the fuzz tests found. Stacked on #45, which adds the fuzz tests and generators these fixes are checked with.

Span protection (from #33):
- Display math on a list marker line was already protected by an earlier fix; a regression test now covers it.
- Inline math never reaches into a link destination, so `[a](/p$$x) and $$` keeps the destination whole.
- A backtick inside inline math is literal and cannot pair with one outside the math.
- A tab after a quote marker counts as columns from the start of the line, as in CommonMark, so `>\ttext` is quoted prose and not quoted code. This also holds for nested quotes.
- A spaced break (`* * *`) no longer opens a list context that hides indented code after it.

Emphasis, quotes and headings (from #34):
- Nested strikethrough resolves inside out in one pass.
- At full verbosity, `Quote:` gets a blank line before a `===` or `---` line, so it cannot become a Setext heading.
- Strong emphasis may hold an isolated literal marker (`**Edit *.py files**`, `__snake_case__`).

Emoji (from #35):
- A lone regional indicator is an emoji, under both policies.

Lists (from #36 and #38):
- An ordered marker that does not start at 1, directly under an item's text, is not a child list. The list is left as written, because speaking it would expose a marker on the next pass.
- A spoken list directly under a kept quote starts with a blank line, so the next pass cannot read it as the quote's lazy continuation and add code labels again.

Fuzz inputs, each shrunk to a few characters (seeds 955 and 1911 no longer reproduced):
- Emphasis markers beside an unmatched backtick are kept, since removing them could merge backtick runs (seed 544).
- No gap is added after `<b` when an emoji is removed, so no HTML tag forms (seed 1485).
- An emoji that is a whole bracket label (`[✨]: …`) is kept, since an empty `[]` stops being link syntax (seed 1588).

One existing test changed: `test_hidden_math_cannot_repair_markers_across_cells` asserted that a table passes through unchanged. Math now never enters a link destination, so nothing pairs across the cells and the table is spoken. The test now asserts what the original fix protected: the output is stable and both destinations are byte-identical.

## How to test

    cd lyre
    uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest
    LYRE_FUZZ_SEED=150 LYRE_FUZZ_CASES=3000 uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest tests/formatter/test_fuzz.py tests/formatter/test_properties.py

`tests/formatter/test_review_followups.py` has one test per finding (its reproduction, formatted twice), plus the shrunk fuzz inputs and the reported seeds.

## Platforms tested

Windows 11, Python 3.14: 3182 passed, 3 skipped. The 3,000-seed sweep passed all 24,005 cases. The golden corpus in #48 is unchanged. Ruff clean.

## Related issues

Closes #43.

title: perf(formatter): reuse stable segmentation and skip impossible protection
issue_body:
## What and why

Reduce repeated work in the speech formatter without changing its output or relaxing the current 100 ms acceptance limit (ADR 0006). This provides additional headroom following the earlier runner-matrix performance failures.

## Changes

- Reuse segmentation from span protection when every block's structural inputs are unchanged.
- Fall back to fresh segmentation for multiline spans, changed quote containers, hidden table pipes, or indentation changes.
- Skip block and inline protection when the input cannot contain a relevant opener.
- Avoid constructing inline pipelines for blocks with no applicable rule.
- Add deterministic work-bound and fallback regressions.

The optimization is isolated on a new branch based on `main`; it does not reopen or modify the merged hook PR.

## How to test

From the repository root:

```sh
uv run --python 3.11 --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml --directory lyre pytest
uv run --python 3.14 --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml --directory lyre pytest
uvx ruff@0.15.10 check .
git diff --check
```

Local results on this branch: **1,973 passed, 3 skipped** on each interpreter. Ruff and whitespace checks pass. The existing 100 ms acceptance test is unchanged and passes locally; remote CI must establish runner-matrix performance.

## Platforms tested

- Windows 11, Python 3.11
- Windows 11, Python 3.14

## Related work

Follow-up to the formatter and hook delivery. No issue is closed by this PR.

title: /a11y slash command
issue_body:
## Subcommands
- `/a11y on` and `/a11y off`: write `enabled` with `ctx.set_config`; confirm in one plain sentence.
- `/a11y status`: one or two plain sentences: on or off, this platform's setting, verbosity.
- `/a11y verbosity brief|normal|full`.
- Unknown input: a one-line usage message.

## Notes
- The setting is profile-wide; the reply says so when turned on in a group chat.
- Check whether a public API lets a plugin detect another loaded `transform_llm_output` plugin. If yes, `/a11y status` warns about it (first non-empty rewrite wins). If no, document the conflict in the README instead.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Works in the classic CLI and in a gateway chat.
- [ ] Setting survives a restart.
- [ ] Replies contain no markdown or emoji.

---
PR Context (#42):
## What and why

Implements the `/a11y` command (#12): a screen-reader user turns Lyre on and off, checks it and changes verbosity from any chat or terminal, and always hears a plain sentence back. **Stacked on #41** (the hook); review the diff against `feat/hook`.

- `lyre/command.py`, registered as `/a11y` with a description and an argument hint:
  - `on`: writes the caller's surface group first (skipped when already on) and `enabled` last, so a failed write never leaves Lyre on without the caller's surface. Replies `Lyre is on. Replies in Telegram will be written for screen readers, starting with the next one.`
  - `off`: writes `enabled=false` only; group choices are kept for next time.
  - `status` (also an empty argument): the three status forms from the spec, naming the caller's surface. Writes nothing.
  - `verbosity brief|normal|full`, and `verbosity` alone reports the current level.
  - `help`, unknown words and extra words after a subcommand give the usage line.
- The caller's surface comes from the handler's `platform` keyword, falling back to `ctx.session_surface()` for `local` or empty, then the hook's surface table. Readable names: Telegram, WhatsApp, the terminal, the terminal UI, the Desktop app, email, scheduled tasks, API and editor sessions; other chats are title-cased (`new_chat` becomes New Chat).
- In a group, channel or thread, `on` and `off` add `This setting applies to every chat on this Hermes profile.`
- Failed writes reply `Lyre could not save that setting. Nothing changed.`, or for `on` `Lyre could not be turned on. Lyre is still off.` (or still on), and log one warning with the key, exception type and traceback (as ADR 0005).
- One case the spec left open: `status` from a surface Lyre never rewrites (a subagent) says `Lyre is on. Verbosity is normal.` without a surface name.

## How to test

    cd lyre
    uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest
    cd ..
    uvx ruff@0.15.10 check .
    hermes plugins validate lyre

New `test_command.py` with a fake context recording writes: AC-1 (Telegram, write order), AC-2 (Desktop opt-in, next Desktop reply rewritten), AC-3, AC-4 (every status form, no writes), AC-5, AC-6, AC-7 (group vs direct vs terminal), AC-8 (state read from saved settings), AC-9 (no `*`, `_`, `#`, `|`, backtick or emoji in any reply), AC-11 (the `enabled` write fails, Lyre stays off and the hook leaves replies alone), plus group-write failure, single-write failures, `on` twice, and a failing `session_surface()`. AC-10 (CLI, TUI and a gateway chat) and Q2 are live checks for the release evidence (#16).

## Platforms tested

Windows 11, Python 3.14, Hermes v0.23.0, locally. CI runs Linux, macOS and Windows on Python 3.11 to 3.14.

## Related issues

Closes #12. Depends on #41 (hook) and the formatter stack.

title: Settings schema and Desktop form
issue_body:
Declare settings in `config_schema` so they validate at load and render as a Desktop form.

## Keys (flat, so the Desktop form uses switches and dropdowns, not a JSON editor)
- `enabled` (bool, default false): the master switch `/a11y on|off` writes.
- One bool per surface group: messaging, email, cli, tui, desktop, api.
- `verbosity` (choices: brief, normal, full; default normal).
- `emoji_policy` (choices, default: status words, remove decorative).
- `table_style` (choices, default: sentences).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every key has a label, description and default.
- [ ] The form renders in Desktop Settings and saving changes the next reply.
- [ ] Invalid values fall back to defaults with a clear log warning.

---
PR Context (#40):
## What and why

Implements the settings spec (#11): every Lyre behaviour is a validated setting with a safe default, editable from `/a11y`, the Desktop Plugins form or `hermes config set`, and read live. Based on `main`; the hook (#10) builds on it.

- `lyre/plugin.yaml`: `config_schema` with 11 flat keys (`enabled`, one switch per surface group, `verbosity`, `emoji_policy`, `table_style`), each with a label and, where useful, a description. `choices` makes the Desktop form render dropdowns.
- `lyre/settings.py`:
  - `load_settings(ctx) -> LyreSettings` reads each key through `ctx.get_config` on every call, with nothing cached. Missing values give the default. Wrong types (`"yes"` for a bool, exact type check, so `1` is not `True`) and values outside `choices` give the default with one `WARNING` per key per process; the value itself is not logged.   - `SCHEMA` mirrors the manifest; a test keeps them equal.

Windows 11, Python 3.14, Hermes v0.23.0, locally. CI runs Linux, macOS and Windows on Python 3.11 to 3.14.

## Behavior (normal verbosity)
- `Table, 3 rows, 4 columns: Name, Price, ...`
- Then each row: `Row 1: Name Alpha, Price 10 dollars, ...`
- Every row and every cell is kept, including empty cells.
- A table over the formatting budget, or a malformed table, passes through unchanged.
- Escaped pipes are handled correctly.
- Table style setting (#11) can change the layout.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A 9-row table keeps every cell.
- [ ] Malformed and oversized tables come out byte-identical.
- [ ] A reply that is only a table.

---
PR Context (#37):
## What and why

Implements task T6 of the formatter spec (#7): tables become sentences a listener can follow and navigate. **Stacked on #36** (then #35, #34, #33); review the diff against `feat/lists`.

- `rules/tables.py`:
  - `Table, 2 rows, 3 columns: Name, Price, Stock.` then `Row 1: Name Alpha, Price $10, Stock 4.` per row, then `End of table.`
  - every cell kept; empty cells say `blank`; short rows padded; a blank header cell is named `Column N`;
  - cells get the inline rules (emphasis, emoji); inline code and URLs stay protected; escaped pipes become `|` in the cell text;
  - pass-through, byte-identical: no separator row, a body row wider than the header, over 50 rows, over 10 columns, any cell over 500 characters, or a mostly non-Latin reply (every sentence form inserts English);
  - `brief`: `Table, 2 rows: ...` and `Row 1: Alpha, $10, 4.`, no end line; `full`: repeats `Columns: ...` before every 10th row; `table_style: unchanged` skips the rule. Both profiles.
- Core: rules can read a protected token's original value (`block.meta["span"]`), used to turn `\|` into `|`.
- The spec's R6 now states the blank-header and non-Latin behaviours.

## How to test

    cd lyre
    uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest
    cd ..
    uvx ruff@0.15.10 check .

New `test_tables.py`: the spec example at every verbosity, AC-1 (nine rows, every cell in order), AC-2 (each pass-through condition), protected cells, short rows, no leading pipes, non-Latin, `unchanged` style, the markdown profile and idempotency. AC-1 and AC-2 pass in the evidence log.

## Platforms tested

Windows 11, Python 3.14, locally. CI runs Linux, macOS and Windows on Python 3.11 to 3.14.

## Related issues

Closes #7. Part of the formatter packet (#3 to #9).

title: Formatter rule: lists
issue_body:
## Behavior (normal verbosity)
- A list is introduced with its size: `3 items.`
- Items are numbered in speech: `1, ...`, `2, ...` (avoid `1.` so markdown clients do not re-render it as a list).
- Nested items say `sub-item`.
- Task-list checkboxes become `(done)` / `(not done)`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests: bullets, numbered, mixed, nested two levels, task lists, list items containing code.

---
PR Context (#36):
## What and why

Implements task T5 of the formatter spec (#6): lists are spoken with their size, numbers and nesting. **Stacked on #35** (then #34, #33); review the diff against `feat/emoji`.

- `rules/lists.py` parses each list block into a tree and emits:
  - a count line before each list (`3 items.`, `2 sub-items.`, `2 level 3 items.`);
  - items as `1, Build` (comma, never a period, so markdown clients do not rebuild the list); ordered lists keep their source numbers;
  - nested items as `sub-item N` and `level N item M`, every nested line indented exactly two spaces;
  - task boxes as `(done)` and `(not done)`;
  - prose continuation lines re-indented to the item's indent; protected code keeps its bytes.
- `brief` drops count lines; `full` says `List, 3 items.`, `Sub-list, 2 items.` and ends with `End of list.`. Mostly non-Latin replies keep numbers but get no English words. Both profiles.
- `spans.py`: a fence opened on an item line (`- ```py`) is now protected; the list rule puts the item number on its own line and the code below it, so the fence starts a line and stays protected on the next pass. The spec's R5 says so.
- Earlier emoji and emphasis tests whose inputs were lists now expect spoken lists.

## How to test

    cd lyre
    uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pyyaml pytest
    cd ..
    uvx ruff@0.15.10 check .

New `test_lists.py`: the spec example at every verbosity, ordered, `)` markers, single item, task lists, loose lists, continuation lines, inline code, deep nesting, non-Latin, code inside items, fences on item lines, AC-18 (three levels with a fence in the deepest item, two passes, no line outside the fence indented 4+ spaces) and idempotency on both profiles.

## Platforms tested

Windows 11, Python 3.14, locally. CI runs Linux, macOS and Windows on Python 3.11 to 3.14.

## Related issues

Closes #6. Part of the formatter packet (#3 to #9).

title: fix(research): research queries returned nothing because of namespace ""
issue_body:
Root cause of empty cited research on the deploy, found after ingesting the corpus (`/api/research/status?verify=true` → 40/40 ready) and still getting `no applicable passage matched` for every crop.

`retrieveLive` passed `namespace: ""` (added with field memory, #91). Vectorize treats that as a literal namespace, so nothing matched. The research vectors have no namespace; `wrangler vectorize query` without a namespace finds them (score 0.99 self-match). Field-memory vectors stay excluded by the existing `corpus` metadata filter (they carry no `corpus` field).

Verified on the test deploy (soilsense-jason) with this commit: /api/research/query returns live passages — corn ksu-li-02 0.833, sorghum 0.828, winter wheat 0.799, soybean sare-11-01 0.718. typecheck, build, 955 tests pass; field-memory isolation test now asserts no namespace + corpus filter.

## Summary
- Diagnose the deployed empty-research symptom as **missing curated ingestion**, not a crop vocabulary, score floor, Gateway or namespace fix: all 40 expected `chunk#crop` IDs are absent. The shared index contained only field-memory vectors.
- Separate bundled corpus configuration from actual readiness. `/api/research/status` now labels ingestion unchecked; `?verify=true` reads all 40 expected IDs in <=20-ID batches, validating default namespace, dimensions and metadata.
- Make the ingestion script poll and fail nonzero unless inventory AND all eight supported crop/feature queries pass (plus unsupported rice returning empty). Add a token-free `--verify-only` path that never POSTs ingestion.
- Keep retrieval algorithms, score floor, engine, field memory, document ingestion and UI unchanged. Document exact coordinator-only repair steps.

## Live evidence (read-only; no deploy, index mutation, migration or secret changes)
- `wrangler vectorize info`: 768 dimensions; initially 36 vectors. Counts grew during concurrent use.
- `list-metadata-index`: both `crop` and `corpus` string indexes exist.
- Complete list/get inventory: 42 vectors, all `field-memory:*`, none with corpus metadata. Direct get-by-ID checks for all 40 curated IDs returned no vectors.
- Finney `POST /api/research/explain` reproduces `research.status=empty`, no passages, `no applicable passage matched` for full-water soybean/cover/corn tags AND rain-fed fallow/winter_wheat/sorghum tags. Top-level generated explanation status can still be live; that is not research readiness.
- The new one-shot `--verify-only` command correctly exits 1 on the currently deployed older Worker instead of trusting bundled `chunks:13`.

title: SLA-VENUE-LICENSE-001 asserts no new requirement under a venue-licence id when the licence question is answered unknown
issue_body:
Surfaced by PR #171's rule-naming audit, which applied the test "does this string state a fact about the answer, when the rule fires on more answers than one" to every string that feature introduces. `SLA-VENUE-LICENSE-001` already ships the same defect for the analogous field.

## The defect

`SLA-VENUE-LICENSE-001`'s trigger includes `venue_license_covers_event_area`, and its output disposition is `NO_NEW_REQUIREMENT_IDENTIFIED`.

When that field is answered an explicit `"unknown"`, `packages/engine/src/conditions.ts` resolves the condition tri-state and the rule is still emitted. So the organizer receives a finding under a **venue-licence** id, asserting that **no new requirement was identified**, on an answer that identifies nothing either way.

Two claims are made from one unanswered question: that the venue licence is the operative instrument, and that nothing further is required.

## Why it matters beyond wording

The disposition is not decoration. `NO_NEW_REQUIREMENT_IDENTIFIED` is one of three dispositions the published ruleset uses, and PR #171 rejected it for a new rule on exactly this ground: it asserts there is no requirement, while the underlying question is recorded as unpublished in either direction.

## What is not being proposed

No fix is proposed here, because the right one is not obvious and touches published regulatory output. The options visible from PR #171's analysis are: an answer-neutral rule id and disposition, a trigger that excludes the explicit unknown, or accepting the current behaviour with the reasoning recorded. Each is a rules change needing verification owner plus engine owner under the change-class table.

## Related

PR #171 renamed its own two proposed rules to `DOB-ASSEMBLY-VENUE-APPROVAL-001` and `-002` for this reason, naming the question and no value of it. That PR reports this defect and deliberately does not fix it, since it is outside its footprint.

title: Say prohibition in the field the engine reads, and block on it when the window has closed
issue_body:
**F-id and spec:** F-102 (`specs/F-102-feasibility-verdict.md`, Acceptance Criterion 10 added and the amendment recorded in its status header). Both halves are product-owner decisions dated 2026-08-08 and recorded in `docs/BASELINE.md`.

Two corrections, in one PR because the first makes the second matter.

## 1. Four draft rules declared the wrong kind, so every prohibition read as "may be required"

`rules/proposals/nyc-rules.v2-full-draft.json` declares four blocking rules. Every one of them said `kind: "eligibility"` and published no `output.disposition`:

| rule | severity | output.status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SAPO-BLOCK-PARTY-INELIGIBLE-001` | blocking | CLASSIFICATION_INELIGIBLE |
| `SAPO-ALCOHOL-PROHIBITION-001` | blocking | PROHIBITED_ELEMENT |
| `NYPD-SOUND-COMMERCIAL-ADVERTISING-PROHIBITED-001` | blocking | PROHIBITED_USE |
| `PARKS-PROPANE-PROHIBITION-001` | blocking | PROHIBITED_ELEMENT |

`severity` and `output.status` are read by no engine code. `DEFAULT_DISPOSITION_BY_RULE_KIND` (`packages/engine/src/proposals.ts:48`) maps `eligibility` to `may_be_required` and already maps `prohibition` to `prohibited_or_ineligible`, so all four resolved to `may_be_required` and every prohibition in the draft was silently a maybe.

This is a rule-authoring error, not a missing capability. It was previously mis-diagnosed as a schema gap; it is not one. The remedy is `kind`, and only `kind`. All four now declare `kind: "prohibition"`. No `output.disposition` is added: the default map is the mechanism, and a per-rule override would say the same thing twice and invite the two to drift.

Nothing else in that file changes. The diff is four lines.

**How it was verified.** The draft does not load through `parseEngineRuleset`, for reasons unrelated to this change: its `is_null` and `lte` trigger operators and its three `derived_values` are outside the engine's condition vocabulary (enumerated in `docs/research/draft-dedupe-cofiring.md` §3.1, on branch `measure/draft-dedupe-cofiring`; that file is not on `main`). So this took the same route that document did: each rule's own declared `kind` was read out of the file and evaluated through `evaluate()` over a ruleset the parser accepts, rather than through the full pipeline. That measures the mapping, which is the whole of what changed. `packages/engine/src/engine.test.ts` pins the mapping itself, `prohibition` resolving to `prohibited_or_ineligible` and `eligibility` to `may_be_required` with no `output.disposition` on either, on a synthetic ruleset. It does not read the draft. An earlier revision did, and that was wrong in one direction that matters: `rules/proposals/*` is PROPOSED in `docs/BASELINE.md`, so an approved engine suite that loads it makes an unapproved artifact a dependency of current-engine CI, where an ordinary draft edit turns the suite red and a second draft file breaks collection for every case in that file. What the four rules declare is regulatory content, reviewed under governance §6 and recorded in `docs/BASELINE.md`; what the engine does with a declared kind is the test's business, and that is the half that is pinned.

**The published ruleset was checked rather than assumed.** `rules/nyc-rules.v2.11.json` carries no rule with this problem and is untouched. It uses neither `severity` nor `output.status` on any rule, so no published rule can be saying something blocking through a field the engine ignores, and both published findings that mean "barred" say so in a field the engine reads: `PARKS-PROPANE-001` by `kind: "prohibition"`, `SAPO-BLOCK-PARTY-ELIG-001` by its own published `disposition: "PROHIBITED_OR_INELIGIBLE"`. That is a test, not a claim.

## 2. A blocked event with a missed deadline read CONDITIONAL

`computeWindowVerdict()` (`packages/engine/src/verdict.ts`) selected its blocking finding from missed findings whose disposition was **exactly** `required`. `prohibited_or_ineligible` is stronger, so a finding that was both barred and past its published filing window fell through to the missed-but-not-blocking branch and the plan rendered CONDITIONAL.

It now blocks on any missed finding at or above `required` in `DISPOSITION_STRENGTH`, which is exported from `findings.ts` rather than restated.

This is pre-existing and is not caused by deduplication: a lone `prohibited_or_ineligible` finding with a closed window and no dedupe key anywhere in it read CONDITIONAL too. It was deliberately kept out of PR #244 as F-102's decision rather than a merge rule, and recorded in the AD-19 entry in `docs/BASELINE.md` and the §8.4 note in `docs/ARCHITECTURE-FUTURE.md`. Those two records describe PR #244 and stand as written; §8.4 gains a dated forward pointer and the new BASELINE entry states the supersession.

### Blast radius, measured before and after

**Zero plans change verdict on the published ruleset, and the reason is structural rather than lucky.**

The sweep: 4,000 intakes over a covering enumeration of all 33 declared intake fields, every declared enum, boolean and multi-select value, and both sides of every published numeric threshold; nine `today` values against a fixed event date `2026-11-15` (`2026-01-05`, and 91/90/89/61/30/14/1/0 days out, so every published window in the ruleset is swept above, on and below its own boundary); three calendar configurations, `holidays: null` as the API deploys it (SPEC-CONFLICT #130), an empty published list as the fixture suite runs it, and a published list with dates inside the swept windows. **108,000 plans per side.**

Both sides are byte-identical: same verdict, same blocking finding, same missed rule ids, same per-finding disposition and deadline status, on all 108,000.

Why zero, rather than a count nobody can interpret: `SAPO-BLOCK-PARTY-ELIG-001` and `PARKS-PROPANE-001` are the only published rules that produce a `prohibited_or_ineligible` finding. They produced 10,464 findings across that sweep, and every single one carried `deadlineStatus: not_applicable`, because neither rule publishes a `deadline` at all and a finding with no published window can never be missed. Nothing else in the ruleset can reach the disposition either: `resolveDisposition()` only ever demotes.

So there is no intake to quote, because there is no plan that moves. The correction is live the moment any published ruleset carries a rule that is both barred and dated.

**Can any of the four draft rules carry a published window?** No. All four publish no `deadline`, so none of them reaches the corrected rule as the draft stands. What item 1 creates is the class, not an instance: a `prohibition`-kind rule is now the natural place to publish a barred requirement that also has a filing window, and item 2 is what stops that plan reading CONDITIONAL when the window has closed.

- `packages/engine/src/verdict.ts` — the blocking filter
- `packages/engine/src/findings.ts` — `DISPOSITION_STRENGTH` exported
- `packages/engine/src/engine.test.ts` — six new cases for the verdict rule, two for the kind-to-disposition mapping, one for the published-ruleset check, one existing expectation amended in place

None. No migration, no endpoint, no enum value, no dependency. `prohibition` and `prohibited_or_ineligible` both already exist in the engine's types and in `DEFAULT_DISPOSITION_BY_RULE_KIND`.

title: mergeFindings keeps the first rule's disposition, so a dedupe group's requirement strength depends on ruleset order
issue_body:
`mergeFindings()` in `packages/engine/src/findings.ts:114` merges a dedupe group with `{ ...first }`, so every scalar field on the merged finding comes from whichever contributing rule the ruleset lists first. `ruleIds`, `notes`, `sources`, `triggeredBy` and `deadlineUnknownFields` are concatenated; `disposition`, `deadlineStatus`, `latestApplyDate`, `deadline`, `name` and `agency` are not merged at all.

Verification status is safe, and deliberately so: `rejectMixedDedupeVerificationStatuses()` (`packages/engine/src/ruleset.ts:665`) refuses at load any ruleset whose dedupe key mixes verification statuses, and `packages/engine/src/engine.test.ts:170` covers it. Every contributing rule in a group therefore shares one status, and the merged scalar is that status rather than an ordering artifact.

Disposition has no equivalent guard, and the shipped ruleset already contains a group that mixes it:

| Rule | Kind | Published disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DOB-TENT-001` | `permit` | default for kind, `required` |
| `DOB-TALL-STRUCTURE-001` | `permit` | `MAY_BE_REQUIRED` |

Both publish `output.dedupe_key: dob-structure` in `rules/nyc-rules.v2.11.json`, and it is the only dedupe key in the file. When both trigger, the merged finding takes `DOB-TENT-001`'s `required` because that rule is listed first. Reordering the two rules in the published file, with no change to any regulatory fact, would render the same merged requirement as `may_be_required` instead.

`resolveDisposition()` widens the reach beyond published dispositions: a rule whose trigger resolves `unknown` is downgraded to `may_be_required` at evaluation time. So even a group whose rules publish one disposition can produce a mixed group at runtime, and the merged value is again the first-listed rule's.

Today's order happens to be the safe one, so there is no organizer-visible defect in the current file. Nothing enforces that. A rules edit that reorders the group, or a new rule joining an existing dedupe key, downgrades a definite requirement to "may be required" in F-202's checklist and in every consumer of `disposition`, silently and with no failing test.

The correct merge is not first-wins in either direction. For disposition the strongest contributing value should win, because either rule triggering means the requirement applies. For verification status the least resolved value should win. A single scalar cannot carry both, which is why the load-time guard exists for status.

Blocks approval of `permit-burden/v1` (`specs/F-103-scope-comparator.md`, `specs/F-502-historical-event-comparison.md`). That metric's `{ definite, unresolved }` split reads `disposition` from the final deduplicated finding, so its stated "unresolved wins" rule is not enforceable from the finding contract as it stands. F-103 records this as an approval blocker and does not authorize the engine change.

Two ways to close it, both engine changes needing verification owner plus engine owner under `docs/DOCUMENTATION-GOVERNANCE.md` §6:

1. A load-time guard on mixed dispositions within a dedupe key, mirroring `rejectMixedDedupeVerificationStatuses()`. Cheapest, and it would reject `nyc.v2.11` as published, so it needs a rules decision about the `dob-structure` group first.
2. Carry per-contributing-rule `disposition` and `verificationStatus` on `FindingSource` (`packages/engine/src/types.ts:253`, currently rule id, citation and URLs only) and merge each field by its own rule instead of by position. This is what lets a consumer apply unresolved-wins across a group.

Found while reviewing #225. Not fixed there: that branch is documentation-only and this is shipped engine behaviour.

`nyc-rules.v2.11.json` has exactly one dedupe key, `dob-structure`, and it mixes three of those six as published:

| Field | DOB-TENT-001 | DOB-TALL-STRUCTURE-001 | Mixed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disposition` | permit-kind default `required` | `MAY_BE_REQUIRED` | yes |
| `deadline` | `business_days_minimum` 15 | none | yes |
| `latestApplyDate` / `deadlineStatus` | derived from the above | derived from the above | yes |
| `name` | DOB permit, tent/canopy over 400 gross sq ft or in place 30+ days | DOB permit, structure over 10 feet tall | yes |
| `agency` | DOB | DOB | no |

Run against the published file on a reachable intake (private venue, `structure_types: [tent_canopy]`, `tent_area_sqft: 500`, `structure_over_10ft_tall: yes`), the merged finding is `required` with `latestApplyDate: 2026-11-13` and `on_track`. Run against the same file with the rules array reversed, and with no regulatory fact changed, it is `may_be_required` with `latestApplyDate: null` and `not_applicable`. That is a live understatement of both what an organizer must file and when the window closes, not a latent one.

No current fixture reaches it. Scenario E and the v2.3 replay both sit at the exact 400 sq ft boundary with `structure_over_10ft_tall: unknown`, where `DOB-TENT-001` resolves unknown and downgrades to `may_be_required` and `DOB-TALL-STRUCTURE-001` publishes `may_be_required` already, so the group does not mix at runtime there.

## What the merge does now

`disposition` is the strongest value any contributing rule publishes, over `no_new_requirement` < `advisory` < `may_be_required` < `required` < `prohibited_or_ineligible`. Rules sharing a dedupe key are several published routes to one requirement, so any one of them applying means the requirement applies, and a weaker value would tell an organizer that a filing they must make merely might apply. A route whose own trigger resolved `unknown` contributes no more than `may_be_required` where the group also holds a route whose own trigger DID resolve at `required` or above, because `ARCHITECTURE-FUTURE.md` 8.4 says a candidate produced by an unknown or official-conflict branch stays conditional and is not promoted by deduplication. Promotion past a resolved route is the whole of what that sentence forbids, so the ceiling is not applied where the group holds no such route.

No single route decides every field, and the round-3 review is what established that. `disposition` is the group's strongest and the filing window is the group's tightest, and those select different routes whenever the strongest route is not also the one that must be filed soonest. So each decided field names its family:

- **Identity**, meaning `kind`, `name`, `agency`, `feeDisplay`, `portalName`, `portalUrl`, `portalInstructions`, `verificationStatus`, `noteText`, `conflictText` and the plain-language heading, reads off the tightest-window route AMONG THOSE CONTRIBUTING THE MERGED DISPOSITION. A line that says an organizer is barred must not name another route's permit or quote its fee and portal.
- **Timeline**, meaning `deadline`, `deadlineDisplay`, `latestApplyDate`, `applyAfterDate`, `deadlineStatus`, `slackDays` and `timelineUnresolvedReason`, reads off the tightest-window route over the WHOLE group, whatever disposition that route contributed. A published window is never dropped for sitting in a weaker disposition tier.
- `lastVerifiedDate` is in neither and stays the earliest across the group, being provenance for the whole line.

Window availability is four levels, not three:

1. a published window that is dated and still open,
2. a published window that has closed,
3. a published window the engine could not date,
4. no published window at all,

with the earlier date deciding between two routes at the same level, and the lower rule id when nothing above separates them.

Levels 3 and 4 are the case the deployed configuration reaches: `apps/api/src/calendar.ts` publishes no holiday list, so `DOB-TENT-001`'s 15-business-day window is real and `not_calculable`, and ranking it below a rule that publishes no window at all would lose the window, its status, its fee and its summary in production. Levels 1 and 3 are the first case the #244 review found: an undatable window used to outrank a datable one, so a group with one computable apply-by date and one uncomputable window bound to the uncomputable route and discarded the other route's date, permit name, fee and portal.

Levels 2 and 3 are the second, and the reason this list changed again. An undatable window used to outrank a closed one, on the reasoning that a closed route is no longer a route. That reasoning assumes the winner is open, and an undatable route is not known to be open: a `research_required` lead time means no agency published one at all, and `deadlines.ts` excludes it from verdict and slack arithmetic. Measured on two routes sharing a key, today 2026-07-22 and event 2026-08-20, the merged line dropped `published_deadline_missed`, the closed route's 2026-06-21 apply-by date and its $500 fee, and read FEASIBLE where `origin/main` reads INFEASIBLE; the `business_days_minimum` sibling under the deployed `holidays: null` calendar took the same plan from INFEASIBLE to CONDITIONAL. A closed window is dated and what it says is that the filing is already late, so it binds ahead of one the engine could not date. Over-warning is the safe direction; understating how soon an organizer must file is the failure this cannot risk. A closed route still never outranks an open one, so a group with one closed and one open route is not missed.

Earlier rather than later because a merged line shows one date, and rendering the later of two published windows leaves an organizer inside the displayed window after the real one has closed. The rule-id tie-break is not a judgement about which rule matters more; it exists so the answer depends on the rules rather than on where they sit in the file. All four levels plus the two tie-breaks are a total order over the group, so the result no longer depends on arrival order. `ruleIds`, `notes`, `sources`, `triggeredBy` and `deadlineUnknownFields` still concatenate in contributing order, which is the approved contract that a merged finding retains every contributing rule and source. `noteText`, `conflictText`, `timelineUnresolvedReason` and the plain-language heading are single-valued published text, so they read from their own family's binding route and fall back through the remaining routes in that family's order rather than being dropped. The heading was the last scalar still resolved by file position: `plan-line.tsx` renders it as the merged line's h3, and its fallback read contributing order, so in a three-route group the title flipped when two summary-publishing rules swapped places with every other decided value identical.

`dedupe()` now collects a group and merges it once instead of folding pairwise into an accumulator. The pairwise fold could not express an order-independent group rule: its tie-breaks would have had to read the accumulator's identity, which is itself a product of arrival order.

## Where 8.4's two guarantees collide

`ARCHITECTURE-FUTURE.md` 8.4 states both that a blocking eligibility or prohibition finding is never erased by a permit finding with the same key, and that candidate requirements produced by official-conflict or unknown branches remain conditional and are not promoted by deduplication. One dedupe group can trigger both: a resolved permit route publishing `required`, and a blocking route on the same key whose own trigger resolved `unknown`. They cannot both hold there.

This resolves it the second way, and says so in 8.4 rather than leaving the collision unstated. `contributedDisposition()` caps an unresolved route at `may_be_required`, `prohibited_or_ineligible` included, so the permit route supplies the merged disposition and the merged line's headline disposition reads `required`. Promoting the blocker instead would tell an organizer their event is ineligible on the strength of a question they never answered, when the answer they have not given may remove the blocker outright.

The carve-out is exactly that collision and no wider, which is the second thing the #244 review found. The cap used to apply to every unknown-triggered route unconditionally, so two conditional blockers on one key, and a conditional blocker beside an advisory, both rendered `may_be_required` where `origin/main` renders `prohibited_or_ineligible`, dropping `plan-line.tsx`'s `line--blocker` styling and its prohibited-finding test id and printing "may be required", with `plan-view.tsx` counting the plan as near-empty. Neither is a permit route erasing a blocker and neither is anything 8.4 speaks to: with nothing resolved at or above the ceiling there is nothing for deduplication to promote the blocker past, so applying the cap demoted a blocking line rather than declining to promote one. The unknown blocker beside a resolved `required` permit is unchanged, which was decided deliberately.

Exactly one thing does not survive there, the merged line's headline `disposition`. What survives: the blocking route stays in `ruleIds`, `sources`, `notes` and `triggeredBy`, its `noteText` survives through the single-valued-text fallback, the field its trigger could not resolve stays a material unknown in `verdictDetail.missingFacts`, and the plan verdict stays CONDITIONAL. Two tests pin both halves, one for the resolved-trigger case where the guarantee holds outright, one for the unresolved case it carves out.

## Authority, and what is not established

No approved artifact states these merged values. `ARCHITECTURE.md:253` says only that findings sharing a `dedupe_key` merge deterministically, retaining every contributing rule and source. The precedence table `ARCHITECTURE-FUTURE.md` 8.4 calls for is Phase 2+ direction and does not exist. Three things 8.4 does settle now are taken as authority: a blocking eligibility or prohibition finding is never erased by a permit finding on the same key, which fixes the top of the disposition order; an unknown or official-conflict branch's candidate is not promoted by deduplication, which caps an unresolved route; and merge order is deterministic rather than incidental array order, which is the defect itself.

The rest is the safe direction for a regulatory product rather than a derived fact, and is labelled as such in the code. It asserts no new regulatory fact: every merged value is some contributing rule's own published value, and every contributing rule stays in `ruleIds` and `sources`, so neither route to the permit is hidden.

Two things are recorded rather than resolved. The `name` and `agency` of a merged group have no basis in any approved artifact at all; tying them to the binding rule is coherent and order-independent, and it is what keeps the shipped output identical, but it is a choice and not a finding. And `feeDisplay`, `portalName`, `portalUrl` and `portalInstructions` follow the identity family, so they belong to the route the headline disposition describes; they were outside the scope of #239 and no group currently mixes them.

Alternatives considered. A load-time guard mirroring `rejectMixedDedupeVerificationStatuses()` is the cheapest and most visible mechanism, and it is unavailable here: `nyc.v2.11` mixes disposition, name and deadline, so the guard would refuse the published ruleset at load and take the engine, api and web down with it. #239 says the same, that it needs a rules decision about `dob-structure` first, and a ruleset edit is not in scope. Leaving a disagreeing group unmerged would return Scenario E to nine findings and contradict `docs/test-scenario-answer-key.md`, which has specified one DOB line since fixtures v3.

## Round 3

Four items, all found by review of this branch's own work, and one of them a design error in the fix rather than a gap in it.

**A closed filing window could be excluded from binding by a filter that ran first.** `mergeGroup()` filtered candidates to the strongest disposition tier and only then ranked by window availability, so `windowAvailability()` never saw a route in a weaker tier. A group holding a closed window under a weaker disposition beside a stronger route publishing no window dropped `published_deadline_missed`, the closed route's apply-by date and its negative slack, and adding a `dedupe_key` to two rules moved the plan verdict with no regulatory fact changing.

The first fix ranked the whole group for every field. That fixed the loss and produced a worse line: name, apply-by date, fee and portal all off the non-blocking route while the disposition came from the blocker, so a barred line quoted a permit and a price. Round 2's own test caught it. Both orderings are hybrids, because the strongest disposition and the tightest window select different routes whenever the strongest route is not the one that must be filed soonest, and the no-hybrid claim this PR previously made was never a property of the merge, only a side effect of disposition happening to be primary. That claim is withdrawn from the code comment, from 8.4 and from the AD-19 record, and replaced by the identity and timeline families above, with every decided field assigned to one of them.

**One loss is not recovered.** Where the merged disposition is `prohibited_or_ineligible` and the group's tightest window has closed, the line carries the missed status, the date and the negative slack, and `verdictDetail.missedRuleIds` carries the rule, but the plan reads CONDITIONAL where the same two rules read INFEASIBLE without a shared key. That is `computeWindowVerdict()`, which selects its blocking finding from missed findings whose disposition is exactly `required`, so a stronger blocking disposition falls through it; a lone `prohibited_or_ineligible` finding with a closed window reads CONDITIONAL today too, merged or not. Widening that is a verdict-semantics change on a shape no published ruleset reaches and is not made here. Recorded in the AD-19 record and in the 8.4 note rather than left to be found.

**A resolved `may_be_required` route demoted a conditional blocker.** The unresolved-route ceiling triggered on any resolved route at or above `may_be_required`, so a resolved MAY_BE_REQUIRED route capped a conditional blocker to `may_be_required` and `plan-line.tsx` dropped the blocker styling and the prohibited-finding marker. Capping there promotes the blocker past nothing, since `may_be_required` is what the cap produces and what the resolved route already said. The cap now needs a resolved route at `required` or above. Four cases pinned: blocker plus resolved advisory, blocker plus resolved `may_be_required` and the blocker alone all keep `prohibited_or_ineligible`; blocker plus resolved `required` still caps, which is the case 8.4 was written for.

**Dependency sequencing keyed on `ruleIds[0]`, which is file order.** After a merge `ruleIds` concatenates in contributing order, so a rule named in `DEPENDENCY_SEQUENCING_BINDINGS` that merged and was not listed first was silently left unsequenced. `applyAfterDate` and `slackDays` are decided values, and F-202 renders the first as the start date while F-203 schedules `dependency_unlocked` at it, so file order decided whether an organizer saw the gate at all. The lookup reads every contributing rule id now, and a test runs the gated rule in both file positions.

## Tests

Written failing first, and they exercise the real path: each builds a dedupe group whose rules differ on a field and asserts the merged finding out of `evaluate()`, not the helper in isolation.

- the strongest disposition wins whichever rule is listed first
- a blocking finding is not erased by a permit finding on the same key, in either listing
- a blocker whose own trigger is unknown does not make the merged line a blocker
- that same unresolved blocker keeps its rule id, source, note text, trigger reason, material unknown and CONDITIONAL verdict, which is the whole of what 8.4's carve-out costs
- every displayed scalar reads off the contributor that supplied the disposition, so a blocked requirement carries no permit's date, fee or portal
- the earlier published filing window wins whichever rule is listed first
- an open window binds over a closed one, and the earliest binds when every route has closed
- a published window that cannot be dated binds over a route that publishes none
- a dated window binds over a route whose window the engine could not date

- a dated rule keeps its window when the other member publishes none, in either listing
- note, conflict and timeline text read off the binding rule rather than the file order
